attack_vector: Direct jailbreak: rule override, persona/role-play, behavioral augmentation (Skeleton Key)
offensive_impact: Critical - policy violation, unauthorized behavior, system-prompt leakage
offensive_likelihood: Very High - black-box, single message, no skill required; ~60% evasion of production shields measured under character injection
defensive_impact: High - input classification is the best-covered control class (GA for models and agents)
defensive_effectiveness: High - Prompt Shields user-prompt detection GA; but probabilistic (classifier)
defensive_maturity: High - mature vendor tooling + open frameworks (PyRIT)
risk_ratio: 1:1 - every offensive technique has a named detection counterpart
residual_risk: Medium - filters are evadable; requires deterministic floor behind them
primary_mitigations: Prompt Shields (block mode) + meta-prompt hardening + output-side policy filters + sanitize invisible Unicode

attack_vector: Hidden instructions in retrieved content (email, docs, web); zero-click chains (EchoLeak pattern)
offensive_impact: Critical - data exfiltration from production LLM systems without user interaction (CVE-2025-32711, CVSS 9.3)
offensive_likelihood: High - single crafted email; exploits retrieval + concatenation of trusted/untrusted context
defensive_impact: Very High - document-attack detection + Spotlighting measured 50%-><2% attack success reduction
defensive_effectiveness: High - Prompt Shields document scanning GA; Spotlighting strongest available (encoding mode)
defensive_maturity: Medium - Spotlighting/datemarking not supported on all agent configurations; DIY implementation often required
risk_ratio: 2:1 - offensive is proven in production; defensive requires correct per-agent configuration to be effective
residual_risk: Medium-High - configuration gaps (agent guardrail overrides, unscanned tool paths) leave real holes
primary_mitigations: Spotlighting/datamarking on every RAG path + document shields at tool-response points + information-flow labels + strict CSP + deterministic exfil-pattern blocking

attack_vector: Gradual escalation referencing model's own replies; benign-input multi-turn attack; automatable (Crescendomation)
offensive_impact: Critical - full safety-alignment bypass; 29-61% higher ASR than prior SOTA on GPT-4, 49-71% on Gemini-Pro
offensive_likelihood: High - black-box, succeeds usually in under ten turns, automatable with API access only
defensive_impact: High - multi-turn filtering passing full conversation history to the detector + AI watchdog trained on adversarial examples
defensive_effectiveness: Medium - representation-level research shows models represent escalating responses as benign; single-turn defenses (circuit breakers) generalize poorly
defensive_maturity: Low-Medium - most deployments still benchmark single-turn only
risk_ratio: 3:1 - attack is mature and automated; the matching defense exists but is not widely deployed
residual_risk: High until multi-turn detection is deployed and measured
primary_mitigations: Conversation-history-aware filtering + trajectory/plan-drift monitoring + output-side cumulative classification + multi-turn ASR benchmarking in CI/CD

attack_vector: Rank-one weight orthogonalization removes refusal direction; uncensored Llama/Mistral-class variants circulate openly
offensive_impact: High - barrier collapse: white-box jailbreak requires no gradients and no harmful examples; uncensored engine for spam/phishing/malware-assist at scale
offensive_likelihood: Medium - requires model download and local inference, but commodity hardware and public tooling make it near-free
defensive_impact: Medium - governance controls (model provenance, egress restriction, local-inference detection) apply, but no classifier sees the model's traffic
defensive_effectiveness: Low - no content policy, no abuse telemetry, no vendor accountability in uncensored self-hosted models
defensive_maturity: Low-Medium - detection is process/egress-level, not content-level
risk_ratio: 3:1 offensive-dominant - the defensive side is governance, not classification
residual_risk: High where open-weight local inference is unmanaged; Medium behind strict model provenance controls
primary_mitigations: Model provenance & approval registry + prohibition of unapproved weights + local-inference egress monitoring + supply-chain artifact verification (hashes, signed manifests)

risk_name: Sensitive Information Disclosure / Shadow AI data loss
attack_vector: Employees pasting PII/source code/IP into unmanaged third-party LLMs; over-broad retrieval; output leakage
offensive_impact: Critical - +USD 670K breach premium for high Shadow AI; 65% PII and 40% IP compromise in Shadow-AI incidents (vs 53%/33% global)
offensive_likelihood: Very High - 1 in 5 organizations already breached via Shadow AI; happens at paste time, outside all telemetry
defensive_impact: Very High - DLP on prompts+outputs, egress controls, approved-tool registry measurably contain the channel; AI/automation in SecOps saves USD 1.9M and 80 days
defensive_effectiveness: High - DLP/SSE/CASB tooling mature; prompts are just another data channel
defensive_maturity: Medium - only 37% of organizations have policies to manage/detect Shadow AI
risk_ratio: 1:3 defensive-dominant - controls exist and pay for themselves; adoption is the gap
residual_risk: Low-Medium once governed; High while unmanaged
primary_mitigations: AI acceptable-use policy + approved-tool registry + DLP treating prompts as data channel + egress policy on AI endpoints + output masking

attack_vector: Hallucinated or injected outputs triggering destructive actions via over-privileged tools (deletions, payments, production writes)
offensive_impact: Critical - destructive actions in production; blast radius = whatever the agent identity can reach
offensive_likelihood: Medium - requires an agent deployment with tools; rising fast (climbed to #3 in OWASP 2026 as agentic deployments grow)
defensive_impact: Very High - least privilege + scoped tools + HITL + tool-call gates cap the blast radius deterministically
defensive_effectiveness: Very High - deterministic controls hold even when every classifier is bypassed
defensive_maturity: Medium - requires per-agent permission review; often inherited too broadly from tool servers
risk_ratio: 1:4 defensive-dominant - fully addressable with structural controls
residual_risk: Low when the deterministic floor is implemented; Critical when agents run with broad permissions
primary_mitigations: Least-privilege scoped tools + keyless/managed identity with short-lived credentials + HITL approval for high-impact actions + tool-call gates + budget/loop ceilings

risk_name: System Prompt Leakage / Hidden Context Exposure
attack_vector: Direct extraction ('repeat everything above'), encoded extraction, guardrail-config reconnaissance
offensive_impact: High - leaks business logic, tool definitions, and internal rules; reconnaissance enabling every higher-severity attack
offensive_likelihood: High - trivial to attempt; often succeeds against unhardened prompts
defensive_impact: High - minimization + extraction-alert monitoring remove the value of the leak
defensive_effectiveness: High - prompt minimization is deterministic; alerting on extraction attempts is mature
defensive_maturity: Medium - requires reviewing what lives in the system prompt
risk_ratio: 1:3 defensive-dominant - the design answer is minimization, not confidentiality
residual_risk: Low when no secrets are in the prompt; High otherwise
primary_mitigations: System-prompt minimization (no secrets/guardrail configs/tool definitions) + meta-prompt extraction refusal + System-Prompt Extraction Attempt alerts to SOC

attack_vector: Base64/ROT13 payloads, invisible Unicode tags (ASCII smuggling), homoglyph substitution, emoji smuggling
offensive_impact: High - 100% evasion measured against some production guardrails (emoji smuggling); payload stays fully readable to the LLM
offensive_likelihood: Medium-High - trivial tooling; often combined with other vectors (extraction, exfiltration)
defensive_impact: High - decode-then-rescan pipelines + Unicode sanitization upstream of classifiers close the gap
defensive_effectiveness: High - sanitization is deterministic and cheap
defensive_maturity: Medium - must be explicitly deployed upstream of every classifier
risk_ratio: 1:2 - deterministic countermeasures exist; they are absent by default
residual_risk: Low once sanitization is deployed; High before it
primary_mitigations: Invisible-Unicode/PUA sanitization upstream of classifiers + decode-then-rescan pipeline + homoglyph normalization + ASCII-smuggling alerts

attack_vector: Compromised model artifacts, poisoned fine-tuning corpora, backdoored weights, unverified third-party integrations
offensive_impact: High - trust failure when a promoted model artifact is not what it claims; backdoors are hard to remediate once shipped
offensive_likelihood: Low-Medium - requires access to training pipelines or artifact distribution, but impact is persistent
defensive_impact: Medium - corpus governance, lineage tracking, artifact verification reduce the surface; poisoning is hard to detect post-hoc
defensive_effectiveness: Medium - provenance/hash verification is deterministic for artifacts, weaker for training data
defensive_maturity: Low-Medium - few organizations verify model artifacts today
risk_ratio: 2:1 offensive-dominant - prevention is cheap; detection post-ship is expensive
residual_risk: Medium with artifact verification; High without
primary_mitigations: Artifact hash/signature verification + signed manifests + corpus lineage + vendor model-change notification + LLM05 adversarial testing

attack_vector: Token/cost exhaustion, resource-intensive requests, runaway agent loops, denial of service of AI-backed services
offensive_impact: High - direct P&L impact and availability loss; attacker-forced cost amplification
offensive_likelihood: Medium - trivially triggered against unthrottled endpoints
defensive_impact: High - quotas, rate limits, and cost ceilings fully contain the risk deterministically
defensive_effectiveness: Very High - deterministic and simple to implement
defensive_maturity: High - standard practice in API design
residual_risk: Low when quotas are enforced; Medium-High before
primary_mitigations: Per-tenant/session token+cost quotas + rate limiting + agent step/tool-call/spend ceilings + anomaly monitoring
